agent.problem: This non-opening story card is five sentences long: the quoted sentence followed by four more sentences. It exceeds the two-sentence limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

agent.problem: The distractor "Stand and fight them" is not false throughout the passage: Joshua and all Israel later turn around and strike down the men of Ai (Joshua 8:21). Use a distractor that never happens in Joshua 8:1-29.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

agent.problem: "Behind them" and "their city" have no antecedent in the question; they rely on the preceding story card to identify the men of Ai. Name the men of Ai in the question itself.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

human.problem: Card 6 says Joshua sends 30,000 men out at night (Joshua 8:3). Card 17 then says "About five thousand men lie in ambush to the west, between Bethel and Ai" (Joshua 8:12) and presents it as the same ambush. A baker sees two different numbers for what reads like one group and gets no signal from the text. The docs say to leave open how two things connect, but they don't say how to present a number that seems to conflict with an earlier one without confusing the baker.
human.question: When a passage gives two numbers that seem to conflict, like 30,000 in Joshua 8:3 and about 5,000 in Joshua 8:12, should Papa Dorin give both exactly as the text does, give only one, or word the second so it doesn't read as a correction of the first, all without explaining the difference?
